description:
`find`'s expression compiler and its parser's real-nesting (`(`/`!`/`-not`) depth.

A flat `-a`/`-o`/`,' chain, however long, parses and compiles as a loop and so never counts
against the nesting guard; only genuine parenthesised or negated nesting does, since that is
the shape that used to recurse once per level in both the parser and `emit`.

cases.name: find nesting: a flat 8000-name -o chain is not nesting
cases.script: mkdir w; cd w; touch f; args=(); for i in $(seq 1 8000); do args+=(-name "nomatch$i" -o); done; find . -maxdepth 1 "${args[@]}" -name f -print; echo status=$?

cases.name: find nesting: 900 levels of real parentheses still compiles
cases.script: mkdir w; cd w; o=$(printf "( %.0s" $(seq 1 900)); c=$(printf ") %.0s" $(seq 1 900)); find . -maxdepth 0 $o -true $c; echo status=$?

cases.name: find nesting: 1001 levels of real parentheses is refused cleanly
cases.script: mkdir w; cd w; o=$(printf "( %.0s" $(seq 1 1001)); c=$(printf ") %.0s" $(seq 1 1001)); find . -maxdepth 0 $o -true $c; echo status=$?

stderr.text: find: maximum nesting level exceeded: deeper nesting is unsupported in bash-tool

expected.reason: fixture: find's own recursive-descent parser and bytecode compiler would overflow the native stack past this depth (see README.md's Limits section); GNU findutils has no comparable limit
